title: Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection
summary: Existing text anomaly detection methods only work at the document level (or on narrow, task-specific token tasks such as spell checking), so they cannot localize which tokens in a text are anomalous. The paper introduces token-level text anomaly detection, releases three token-annotated benchmarks (SMS_Spam with injected character corruption, Restaurant Review semantic anomalies, Grammar errors), and proposes TokenCore, which builds a memory bank of normal word-level token embeddings (BERT-base-uncased embeddings aggregated by element-wise max pooling over subwords) and scores each test token by its nearest-neighbor distance, aggregating token scores by mean for document-level scores. TokenCore achieves the best average token-level AUROC (0.7145) and document-level AUROC (0.7335) among 7 methods, ranking first at token level on Review (0.8271) and Grammar (0.6371) and at document level on Review (0.9594), while ECOD/iForest remain better on the character-corruption SMS_Spam token-level task.

why: The authors released the method code (TokenCore.py: memory bank + nearest-neighbor token scoring), the alignment/annotation utilities (align.py, tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py) and all three annotated datasets locally in data/ (grammar .npy/.json, restaurant_review, sms_spam), so the core logic can be kept verbatim. What is NOT released is a runnable entrypoint: the only end-to-end artifact is Demo.ipynb (with frozen outputs), there is no requirements.txt, and TokenCore.py consumes precomputed token-embedding matrices, so the BERT-base-uncased embedding extraction, the 50/50 split and the token-level AUROC computation have to be rebuilt as a script from the notebook before the target number for Grammar (C1) can be produced. Keep authors' logic, rebuild the missing driver.
est_runtime: ~25-35 min wall clock on 22 CPU cores / 15.4 GB RAM: ~10 min installing torch (CPU wheel), transformers, scikit-learn; ~1 min BERT-base download; ~1-3 min BERT forward pass over 300 short Grammar documents; seconds for the max-pooling, memory-bank build and brute-force nearest-neighbor scoring; plus the driver-script rewrite from the notebook and one clean end-to-end re-run.
blockers: no dependency file: torch/transformers/sklearn/numpy must be pinned by hand (works on Python 3.12)
TokenCore.py takes embedding matrices only; the BERT max-pooling-over-subwords front-end exists only inside the notebook, so the pipeline must be extracted into a script
Demo.ipynb is 3.8 MB of stored outputs; it must be rewritten/cleared before execution
no GPU on this machine (BERT-base CPU inference only, which is acceptable at this scale)

Grammar token-level AUROC is computed over very few anomalous tokens (~15 anomalous docs in the test half), and the split is random, so the absolute value 0.6371 will depend on the split seed and may drift

approach: This is a partial_release reproduction of claim C1: TokenCore's token-level AUROC on the Grammar benchmark (0.6371, tolerance ±0.02 absolute). We clone the authors' repo, keep TokenCore.py/align.py/json_to_npy.py verbatim, and rebuild only the missing driver that Demo.ipynb used to hide: read the released grammar annotations (data/grammar_correction_labeled.json and data/grammar.npy), build the 300-document corpus (270 normal / 30 anomalous, R10), take 50% of the normal documents as the memory-bank training set (R6, A8), run BERT-base-uncased over the remaining normal + anomalous documents, max-pool subword embeddings into word units aligned with the gold word-level token labels (Eq. 1, R2/R9, A3/A4), fit the authors' TextCore memory bank on normal-training token embeddings only (R3, A2), score every test token by Euclidean nearest-neighbour distance (Eq. 2, R4, A1/A9), and compute pooled token-level AUROC/AUPRC plus the mean-aggregated document-level scores (Eq. 3, R5, A5). The paper value is a single split-free number, so the only real drift risk is split randomness on 300 short documents; we therefore report a primary seeded run plus a small multi-seed spread so the ±0.02 band can be interpreted. Only the Grammar dataset is needed for C1, but the same driver is written so that running it on restaurant_review / sms_spam later costs nothing extra.
steps: Clone https://github.com/charles-cao/TokenCore.git into ./TokenCore and record the commit hash; do not modify TokenCore.py, align.py or tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py.

Create a venv/conda env on Python 3.12 and pip install torch (CPU wheel from the default index), transformers, numpy, scikit-learn, tqdm, requests; write the resolved versions into requirements.txt (the file the README references but the repo lacks).

Run src/inspect_data.py: dump shapes/dtypes/keys of data/grammar.npy and the JSON schema of data/grammar_correction_labeled.json, and print the actual class/function signatures of TokenCore.py and align.py. Decide the exact field names for words, token labels and document labels, and confirm the .npy is a token/label array rather than precomputed embeddings (43 KB is far too small for 300x768 floats).

Implement src/data_grammar.py against the inspected schema; load all 300 Grammar documents and hard-assert 300 documents / 270 normal / 30 anomalous (10% rate, R10) and consistency of the document labels with the token labels (R11).

Implement the split: with seed 0, shuffle the 270 normal documents, take the first 135 as the memory-bank training set; the test set is the other 135 normal documents plus all 30 anomalous documents (165 docs). Export the token-level gold labels for every test token.

Implement src/embed_bert.py: tokenize with BertTokenizerFast(return_offsets_mapping / word_ids), run BertModel in eval() with torch.no_grad() in batches of 32, max_length 128, take last_hidden_state, drop special tokens, and element-wise max-pool subwords per word unit. Assert a 1:1 map between produced word units and the gold word tokens in the annotated JSON; if align.py exposes an alignment helper, call it instead of re-implementing.

Implement src/detector.py: import the authors' TokenCore (use the real class name found by inspect_data.py, README shows both TokenCore and TextCore) and its fit / decision_function, fit on the normal-training token embedding matrix (no anomalous tokens, R3) and score the test token embeddings (R4).

Implement src/evaluate.py: token-level AUROC/AUPRC pooled over all test tokens (micro), document-level scores as the per-document mean of token scores (R5) and their AUROC/AUPRC, plus a random-score control (expected AUROC ~0.5) to validate the metric plumbing.
Wire reproduce.py to run the whole chain end-to-end; run the smoke configuration first (see smoke_test) and confirm all assertions on counts and shapes pass.
Run the intermediate checks (see intermediate_checks) before the full run.

Full run: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --seed 0 (CPU-only BERT inference over 300 short sentences, seconds for the memory bank and brute-force L2 nearest-neighbour search). Write results/metrics.json.

If |token_auroc_grammar - 0.6371| > 0.02, re-run with seeds 1 and 2 and inspect sensitivity: report the per-seed values and mean/std, and check the highest-risk choices first (A5 micro vs per-document AUROC, A1/A9 Euclidean on unnormalized embeddings, A4 whether punctuation units are scored).
Write the final results/metrics.json containing the primary value, the multi-seed spread, the target, the tolerance band and an explicit pass/fail flag.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --smoke --seed 0 -> loads the released grammar annotations, keeps only the first 8 normal + first 2 anomalous documents (forcing the split so both sides are non-empty), runs one BERT-base forward pass over those 10 documents, max-pools subwords, builds a ~100-200 entry memory bank, scores the test tokens, and prints token_auroc/token_auprc plus every shape (n_docs, n_word_units, n_bank_tokens, n_test_tokens, n_positive_tokens). Success = no exception, finite scores, 1:1 alignment between word units and gold tokens, and AUROC in [0,1]. This exercises every stage of the data flow in under a minute.
intermediate_checks: Dataset size and label rate: exactly 300 documents, 270 normal (token_labels all 0) and 30 anomalous (>=1 token_label = 1) = 10% anomaly rate (R10); stop if the released file deviates.
Document/token label consistency: every document with at least one 1 token has doc_label 1 and vice versa (R11).

Token-level class balance: report total tokens, total anomalous tokens and their fraction across all 300 docs, and across the 165 test docs; sanity expectation is a few percent (the contract quotes token AUPRC ~0.04 for Grammar, which is roughly the positive rate) and only a handful of positives, so AUROC variance across seeds will be large - this justifies the ±0.02 band.
Alignment coverage: fraction of gold word tokens that receive a BERT word unit (target 1.0); log any word that tokenizes to zero subwords or overflows max_length=128.
Split sizes: 135 normal training docs and 135 normal + 30 anomalous test docs with seed 0; training set contains zero anomalous tokens (R3).

Memory bank size: n_bank_tokens should equal the total number of word units in the 135 normal training documents (report it; expect a few thousand) - a much smaller number means documents were dropped silently.

Parameter/embedding check: assert the token embedding width is 768 and that the pooling really is element-wise max (a max-pooled vector must equal the coordinate-wise max of its subword vectors on a hand-checked example).

Sanity baseline: random token scores give AUROC ~0.5 and AUPRC ~positive rate; TokenCore scores on the training tokens themselves (excluding self-matches) give near-zero distances, confirming the nearest-neighbour direction (higher distance = more anomalous, R4).
Metric parity: verify the AUROC/AUPRC implementation against sklearn.roc_auc_score / average_precision_score on synthetic labels, so the 0.6371 comparison cannot fail for plumbing reasons.
budget_plan: Total ~30-35 min on 22 CPU cores / 15.4 GB RAM. Setup 10 min: clone the repo (<1 min) and pip install the CPU torch wheel plus transformers/scikit-learn (~8-9 min, ~5 GB, the dominant cost). Reconnaissance 3 min: inspect_data.py plus reading TokenCore.py/align.py and the JSON schema. Implementation 8 min: data_grammar.py, embed_bert.py, detector.py, evaluate.py, reproduce.py, requirements.txt. Smoke 2 min: 10-document subset end-to-end. Intermediate checks 2 min: counts, rates, alignment coverage, bank size, metric parity. Full run 3-4 min: one BERT-base forward pass over 300 short Grammar sentences on CPU (1-3 min) plus seconds of max-pooling and brute-force L2 nearest-neighbour scoring. Verification 3 min: compare against 0.6371 with the ±0.02 band, and if out of band spend up to 5 more minutes on seeds 1 and 2 and on the highest-risk assumptions (A5, A1/A9, A4). Keep ~3 min slack; only the Grammar dataset is run, so no SMS_Spam/Review time is spent.

    4| class TokenCore:
    5|     """
    6|     TokenCore anomaly detector based on nearest neighbor distances
    7|     """
    8|     def __init__(self, n_neighbors=1, aggregation='max'):
    9|         """
   10|         Parameters
   11|         ----------
   12|         n_neighbors : int, default=1
   13|             Number of neighbors to use
   14|         aggregation : str, default='mean'
   15|             How to aggregate distances when n_neighbors > 1
   16|             Options: 'mean', 'max', 'min', 'median'
   17|         """
   18|         self.n_neighbors = n_neighbors
   19|         self.aggregation = aggregation
   20|         self.nbrs = None
   21|         
   22|     def fit(self, X):
   23|         """
   24|         Fit the model using X as training data
   25|         
   26|         Parameters
   27|         ----------
   28|         X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
   29|             Training data
   30|             
   31|         Returns
   32|         -------
   33|         self : object
   34|             Fitted estimator
   35|         """
   36|         self.nbrs = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=self.n_neighbors).fit(X)
   37|         return self
   38|     
   39|     def decision_function(self, X):
   40|         """
   41|         Compute anomaly scores for samples in X
   42|         
   43|         Parameters
   44|         ----------
   45|         X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
   46|             Test data
   47|             
   48|         Returns
   49|         -------
   50|         scores : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
   51|             Anomaly scores (higher means more anomalous)
   52|         """
   53|         distances, _ = self.nbrs.kneighbors(X)
   54|         
   55|         # If n_neighbors == 1, distances is (n_samples, 1), just flatten
   56|         if self.n_neighbors == 1:
   57|             scores = distances.flatten()
   58|         else:
   59|             # Aggregate multiple neighbor distances
   60|             if self.aggregation == 'mean':
   61|                 scores = np.mean(distances, axis=1)
   62|             elif self.aggregation == 'max':
   63|                 scores = np.max(distances, axis=1)
   64|             elif self.aggregation == 'min':
   65|                 scores = np.min(distances, axis=1)
   66|             elif self.aggregation == 'median':
   67|                 scores = np.median(distances, axis=1)
   68|             else:
   69|                 raise ValueError(f"Unknown aggregation method: {self.aggregation}")
   70|         
   71|         return scores

    1| # TokenCore
    2| 
    3| Official code and datasets for the paper
    4| **[Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection](https://huggingface.co/papers/2601.13644)** (WWW '26).
    5| 
    6| TokenCore is a memory-bank method for **token-level text anomaly detection**: instead of only flagging whole documents as anomalous, it localizes *which specific tokens* are anomalous. It builds a memory bank of normal token embeddings and scores each test token by its distance to the nearest normal neighbor, then aggregates token scores to obtain document-level scores.
    7| 
    8| ## Datasets
    9| 
   10| The three benchmark datasets are hosted on the Hugging Face Hub:
   11| 
   12| 👉 **[https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD)**
   13| 
   14| Each dataset provides both document-level and token-level anomaly annotations.
   15| 
   16| | Dataset | Anomaly type | Documents | Anomalies | Rate |
   17| |---|---|---|---|---|
   18| | SMS Spam | Character-level (corrupted sequences) | 4,518 | 393 | 8.7% |
   19| | Restaurant Review | Semantic (negative sentiment) | 1,100 | 50 | 4.5% |
   20| | Grammar Correction | Grammatical errors | 300 | 30 | 10% |
   21| 
   22| A local copy is also available in the `data/` folder.
   23| 
   24| ## Installation
   25| 
   26| ```bash
   27| git clone https://github.com/charles-cao/TokenCore.git
   28| cd TokenCore
   29| pip install -r requirements.txt
   30| ```
   31| 
   32| ## Quick Start
   33| 
   34| ```python
   35| from TokenCore import TextCore
   36| 
   37| model = TokenCore()
   38| 
   39| # Fit on normal token embeddings
   40| model.fit(X_train)
   41| 
   42| # Get token-level anomaly scores
   43| scores = model.decision_function(X_test)
   44| ```
   45| 
   46| `X_train` and `X_test` are token embedding matrices (e.g. BERT embeddings with max-pooling over subwords). See `Demo.ipynb` for the full pipeline, including embedding extraction, token-level scoring, and document-level aggregation.

import os, time
cache = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE", ".")

os.makedirs(hf, exist_ok=True)
os.environ["HF_HOME"] = hf

import torch
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel

t = time.time()
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("bert-base-uncased", cache_dir=hf)
mdl = AutoModel.from_pretrained("bert-base-uncased", cache_dir=hf)
print("loaded", time.time() - t)
enc = tok(["I", "go", "to", "the", "store", "everyday", "."], is_split_into_words=True,
          return_tensors="pt", truncation=True, max_length=128)
print(enc.word_ids(batch_index=0))
with torch.no_grad():
    out = mdl(input_ids=enc["input_ids"], attention_mask=enc["attention_mask"])
print(out.last_hidden_state.shape)
print("total", time.time() - t)

"""Load the released Grammar Correction benchmark (TokenCore repo, data/grammar.npy).

Schema (verified): dict with keys 'sentences', 'tokens', 'labels'
  sentences[i] = [sentence_string]      (kept only for reference)
  tokens[i]    = list of word-level tokens (already word-segmented, punctuation kept)
  labels[i]    = list of 0/1 word-level anomaly labels, len == len(tokens[i])
Document label = 1 iff the document contains at least one anomalous token
(paper Definition 2 / contract R11).
"""
import numpy as np

DATA_PATH = "repo/data/grammar.npy"


def load_grammar(path=DATA_PATH):
    raw = np.load(path, allow_pickle=True).item()
    docs = []
    for i, (tokens, labels) in enumerate(zip(raw["tokens"], raw["labels"])):
        tokens = [str(t) for t in tokens]
        labels = [int(x) for x in labels]
        assert len(tokens) == len(labels), (i, len(tokens), len(labels))
        assert len(tokens) > 0, i
        doc_label = 1 if any(labels) else 0
        docs.append(
            {
                "doc_id": i,
                "sentence": raw["sentences"][i][0],
                "tokens": tokens,
                "labels": labels,
                "doc_label": doc_label,
            }
        )
    return docs


def check_dataset(docs):
    """Hard checks from the paper (Sec. 4): 300 documents, 30 anomalous, 10%."""
    n = len(docs)
    n_anom = sum(d["doc_label"] for d in docs)
    n_pos_tok = sum(sum(d["labels"]) for d in docs)
    n_tok = sum(len(d["tokens"]) for d in docs)
    checks = {
        "n_docs": n,
        "n_normal_docs": n - n_anom,
        "n_anomalous_docs": n_anom,
        "anomaly_rate": n_anom / n,
        "n_tokens": n_tok,
        "n_positive_tokens": n_pos_tok,
        "positive_token_rate": n_pos_tok / n_tok,
    }
    assert n == 300, f"expected 300 documents, got {n}"
    assert n_anom == 30, f"expected 30 anomalous documents, got {n_anom}"
    for d in docs:
        assert d["doc_label"] == (1 if any(d["labels"]) else 0)
    return checks


def split_docs(docs, seed=0, protocol="50pct_normal"):
    """50/50 split of the NORMAL documents (paper Sec. 6.1 / contract R6).

    protocol='50pct_normal': train = 50% of normal docs, test = remaining normal
        docs + every anomalous doc.
    protocol='50pct_all' (sensitivity only): 50% of *all* documents are drawn as
        the training pool and only their normal members form the memory bank;
        the test set is the rest (normal + anomalous).  This is what the authors'
        frozen demo.ipynb looks like it did for Restaurant Review (550 train
        sentences out of 1,100 documents), and it is reported as a sensitivity.
    """
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    normal = [d for d in docs if d["doc_label"] == 0]
    anom = [d for d in docs if d["doc_label"] == 1]
    if protocol == "50pct_normal":
        perm = rng.permutation(len(normal))
        k = len(normal) // 2
        train = [normal[i] for i in perm[:k]]
        test_normal = [normal[i] for i in perm[k:]]
        test = test_normal + anom
    elif protocol == "50pct_all":
        perm = rng.permutation(len(docs))
        k = len(docs) // 2
        train_pool = [docs[i] for i in perm[:k]]
        test_pool = [docs[i] for i in perm[k:]]
        train = [d for d in train_pool if d["doc_label"] == 0]
        test = test_pool
    else:
        raise ValueError(protocol)
    rng.shuffle(test)
    return train, test

"""BERT-base-uncased word-level embedding front-end (paper Sec. 5, Eq. 1).

This is the missing piece of the release: the authors' align.py only extracts
embeddings one sentence at a time (and prints every alignment), and Demo.ipynb
used it directly.  The pooling semantics below are copied from
align.extract_word_embeddings: last hidden state -> drop [CLS]/[SEP]/[PAD] ->
group subwords by word_ids() -> element-wise MAX over the subword vectors of a
word.  A parity check against align.extract_word_embeddings is executed by
verify_parity().
"""
import numpy as np
import torch
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel

MAX_LEN = 128
BATCH = 32


def load_model(model_name="bert-base-uncased", cache_dir=None):
    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name, cache_dir=cache_dir)
    mdl = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name, cache_dir=cache_dir)
    mdl.eval()
    return tok, mdl


def pool_word_units(last_hidden_state, word_ids, n_words):
    """[n_subwords, 768] + word_ids -> [n_words, 768] element-wise max pooling."""
    out = np.zeros((n_words, last_hidden_state.shape[-1]), dtype=np.float32)
    seen = np.zeros(n_words, dtype=bool)
    hs = last_hidden_state
    for pos, wid in enumerate(word_ids):
        if wid is None:
            continue
        if not seen[wid]:
            out[wid] = hs[pos]
            seen[wid] = True
        else:
            out[wid] = np.maximum(out[wid], hs[pos])
    return out, seen


def embed_documents(docs, tok, mdl, max_len=MAX_LEN, batch_size=BATCH, n_threads=8):
    """Return list of dicts {doc_id, emb [n_words,768], labels, doc_label}."""
    torch.set_num_threads(n_threads)
    results = []
    for start in range(0, len(docs), batch_size):
        batch = docs[start : start + batch_size]
        enc = tok(
            [d["tokens"] for d in batch],
            is_split_into_words=True,
            return_tensors="pt",
            truncation=True,
            max_length=max_len,
            padding=True,
        )
        with torch.no_grad():
            out = mdl(input_ids=enc["input_ids"], attention_mask=enc["attention_mask"])
        hidden = out.last_hidden_state.numpy().astype(np.float32)
        for j, d in enumerate(batch):
            word_ids = enc.word_ids(batch_index=j)
            n_words = len(d["tokens"])
            emb, seen = pool_word_units(hidden[j], word_ids, n_words)
            # contract R9: every gold word must receive a word unit
            assert seen.all(), (d["doc_id"], int(seen.sum()), n_words)
            results.append(
                {
                    "doc_id": d["doc_id"],
                    "emb": emb,
                    "labels": d["labels"],
                    "doc_label": d["doc_label"],
                }
            )
    return results


def verify_parity(embedded, docs, model_name, cache_dir, n_check=3):
    """Check the batched max pooling against the authors' align.py, verbatim."""
    import sys

    sys.path.insert(0, "repo")
    from align import extract_word_embeddings  # authors' file, unmodified

    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name, cache_dir=cache_dir)
    mdl = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name, cache_dir=cache_dir)
    by_id = {e["doc_id"]: e for e in embedded}
    sample = docs[:n_check]
    # align.py prints a lot; silence it for the check
    import contextlib, io

    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
        ref = extract_word_embeddings(
            model=mdl,
            tokenizer=tok,
            all_tokens=[d["tokens"] for d in sample],
            all_labels=[d["labels"] for d in sample],
            model_name=model_name,
            local_cache_dir=cache_dir,
            device="cpu",
        )
    max_diff = 0.0
    for d, ref_sent in zip(sample, ref):
        mine = by_id[d["doc_id"]]["emb"]
        assert len(ref_sent) == mine.shape[0], (len(ref_sent), mine.shape)
        r = np.stack([item["embedding"] for item in ref_sent])
        max_diff = max(max_diff, float(np.abs(r - mine).max()))
    return max_diff

"""Thin adapter over the authors' unmodified repo/TokenCore.py.

The authors' class is imported from the released file itself (nothing is
re-implemented); the adapter only enforces the paper's contract:
  * fit() on the memory bank of normal-training token embeddings (R3)
  * decision_function() = distance to nearest neighbour in the bank (R4)
"""
import sys
import os

import numpy as np

REPO_DIR = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), "repo")
if REPO_DIR not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, REPO_DIR)

from TokenCore import TokenCore  # noqa: E402  (authors' released implementation)


class MemoryBankScorer:
    def __init__(self):
        self.model = TokenCore(n_neighbors=1)

    def fit(self, bank_X):
        bank_X = np.asarray(bank_X, dtype=np.float32)
        assert bank_X.ndim == 2 and bank_X.shape[1] == 768, bank_X.shape
        self.model.fit(bank_X)
        self.n_bank = bank_X.shape[0]
        return self

    def score(self, test_X):
        test_X = np.asarray(test_X, dtype=np.float32)
        assert test_X.ndim == 2 and test_X.shape[1] == 768, test_X.shape
        return np.asarray(self.model.decision_function(test_X), dtype=np.float64)

"""Metric layer: token-level (micro, all test tokens pooled) and document-level
(mean aggregation of token scores, Eq. 3) AUROC/AUPRC.  Contract R5/R7."""
import numpy as np
from sklearn.metrics import average_precision_score, roc_auc_score


def token_metrics(token_scores, token_labels):
    token_scores = np.asarray(token_scores, dtype=np.float64)
    token_labels = np.asarray(token_labels, dtype=np.int64)
    return {
        "auroc": float(roc_auc_score(token_labels, token_scores)),
        "auprc": float(average_precision_score(token_labels, token_scores)),
        "n_tokens": int(token_labels.size),
        "n_positive_tokens": int(token_labels.sum()),
        "positive_rate": float(token_labels.mean()),
    }


def doc_scores_from_tokens(embedded_docs, token_scores):
    """Eq. 3: document score = arithmetic mean of its token scores."""
    out, labels = [], []
    pos = 0
    for e in embedded_docs:
        n = e["emb"].shape[0]
        out.append(float(np.mean(token_scores[pos : pos + n])))
        labels.append(int(e["doc_label"]))
        pos += n
    assert pos == len(token_scores)
    return np.array(out), np.array(labels)


def doc_metrics(doc_scores, doc_labels):
    return {
        "auroc": float(roc_auc_score(doc_labels, doc_scores)),
        "auprc": float(average_precision_score(doc_labels, doc_scores)),
        "n_docs": int(len(doc_labels)),
        "n_positive_docs": int(np.asarray(doc_labels).sum()),
    }


def metric_parity_check():
    """Guard against plumbing errors: sklearn sanity on synthetic scores."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(123)
    y = (rng.random(500) < 0.2).astype(int)
    good = y + rng.normal(0, 1, 500) * 2
    assert abs(token_metrics(good, y)["auroc"] - roc_auc_score(y, good)) < 1e-12
    rand = token_metrics(rng.random(500), y)
    assert 0.35 < rand["auroc"] < 0.65, rand
    assert abs(rand["auprc"] - y.mean()) < 0.08, rand
    return {"random_auroc": rand["auroc"], "random_auprc": rand["auprc"]}

"""Reproduce TokenCore's token-level Grammar results (paper Table 1, C1/C2).

Pipeline (authors' code kept verbatim, only the missing driver rebuilt):
  data/grammar.npy (released token/label annotations)
    -> BERT-base-uncased contextual embeddings
    -> element-wise max pooling over the subwords of each gold word (Eq. 1)
    -> memory bank of all word embeddings of the 50% normal training docs
    -> per-test-token nearest-neighbour distance in the authors' TokenCore
    -> token-level AUROC / AUPRC (micro) and document-level mean aggregation.

Usage:
  python reproduce.py                 # full run (seeds 0..9, paper protocol)
  python reproduce.py --smoke         # tiny 10-document smoke test
  python reproduce.py --sensitivity   # also report the alternative split
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import time

import numpy as np

# Keep the HuggingFace model cache in the shared data cache (checked first).
CACHE = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE", os.path.join(os.getcwd(), ".cache"))
HF_HOME = os.path.join(CACHE, "hf")
os.makedirs(HF_HOME, exist_ok=True)
os.environ.setdefault("HF_HOME", HF_HOME)
os.environ.setdefault("HF_HUB_DISABLE_SYMLINKS_WARNING", "1")

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

from src import data_grammar, detector, embed_bert, evaluate  # noqa: E402


def run_config(docs, embedded, tok, mdl, seeds, protocol, model_name, cache_dir, log):
    by_id = {e["doc_id"]: e for e in embedded}
    per_seed = []
    for seed in seeds:
        train, test = data_grammar.split_docs(docs, seed=seed, protocol=protocol)
        train_ids = [d["doc_id"] for d in train]
        test_ids = [d["doc_id"] for d in test]

        bank = np.concatenate([by_id[i]["emb"] for i in train_ids], axis=0)
        # contract R3: the memory bank must not contain any anomalous token
        assert sum(sum(by_id[i]["labels"]) for i in train_ids) == 0

        scorer = detector.MemoryBankScorer().fit(bank)
        test_emb = [by_id[i] for i in test_ids]
        # per-document scoring, then flatten (order matches doc_scores_from_tokens)
        token_scores, token_labels = [], []
        for e in test_emb:
            token_scores.append(scorer.score(e["emb"]))
            token_labels.extend(e["labels"])
        token_scores = np.concatenate(token_scores)
        tm = evaluate.token_metrics(token_scores, token_labels)
        ds, dl = evaluate.doc_scores_from_tokens(test_emb, token_scores)
        dm = evaluate.doc_metrics(ds, dl)
        rec = {
            "seed": seed,
            "n_train_docs": len(train_ids),
            "n_test_docs": len(test_ids),
            "n_bank_tokens": int(bank.shape[0]),

            f"({tm['n_positive_tokens']}/{tm['n_tokens']} pos)"

"""Scratch exploration (not part of the deliverable): compare backbone / distance
variants for the Grammar token-level AUROC.  Writes cached embeddings to the
shared data cache so re-runs are cheap."""
import os, sys, json, time
import numpy as np

CACHE = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE", ".cache")
HF = os.path.join(CACHE, "hf")
os.environ.setdefault("HF_HOME", HF)
os.environ.setdefault("HF_HUB_DISABLE_SYMLINKS_WARNING", "1")
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
import transformers
transformers.utils.logging.set_verbosity_error()
from src import data_grammar, embed_bert, detector, evaluate

EMB_CACHE = os.path.join(CACHE, "grammar_emb")


def get_embeddings(model_name):
    os.makedirs(EMB_CACHE, exist_ok=True)
    key = model_name.replace("/", "_")
    path = os.path.join(EMB_CACHE, key + ".npz")
    docs = data_grammar.load_grammar()
    if os.path.exists(path):
        z = np.load(path, allow_pickle=True)
        data = z["data"].item()
        return docs, data
    tok, mdl = embed_bert.load_model(model_name, cache_dir=HF)
    t = time.time()
    emb = embed_bert.embed_documents(docs, tok, mdl)
    print(f"[{model_name}] embedded in {time.time()-t:.1f}s")
    np.savez_compressed(path, data=np.array(emb, dtype=object))
    return docs, emb


def variants(X):
    yield "raw", X
    n = X / (np.linalg.norm(X, axis=1, keepdims=True) + 1e-12)
    yield "l2norm", n


def score_hist_auroc(docs, emb, seed, protocol, mode):
    by_id = {e["doc_id"]: e for e in emb}
    train, test = data_grammar.split_docs(docs, seed=seed, protocol=protocol)
    bank = np.concatenate([by_id[d["doc_id"]]["emb"] for d in train]).astype(np.float32)
    tests = [by_id[d["doc_id"]] for d in test]
    if mode == "raw":
        pass
    elif mode == "l2norm":
        bank = bank / (np.linalg.norm(bank, axis=1, keepdims=True) + 1e-12)
    sc = detector.MemoryBankScorer().fit(bank)
    scores, labels = [], []
    for e in tests:
        x = e["emb"].astype(np.float32)
        if mode == "l2norm":
            x = x / (np.linalg.norm(x, axis=1, keepdims=True) + 1e-12)
        scores.append(sc.score(x))
        labels.extend(e["labels"])
    scores = np.concatenate(scores)
    tm = evaluate.token_metrics(scores, labels)
    ds, dl = evaluate.doc_scores_from_tokens(tests, scores)
    dm = evaluate.doc_metrics(ds, dl)
    return tm, dm


if __name__ == "__main__":
    models = sys.argv[1].split(",") if len(sys.argv) > 1 else ["bert-base-uncased"]
    for mn in models:
        docs, emb = get_embeddings(mn)
        for mode in ["raw", "l2norm"]:
            for protocol in ["50pct_normal", "50pct_all"]:
                au, ap, da = [], [], []
                for seed in range(5):
                    tm, dm = score_hist_auroc(docs, emb, seed, protocol, mode)
                    au.append(tm["auroc"]); ap.append(tm["auprc"]); da.append(dm["auroc"])
                print(f"{mn:20s} {mode:7s} {protocol:12s} tokenAUROC={np.mean(au):.4f}±{np.std(au):.4f} "
                      f"tokenAUPRC={np.mean(ap):.4f} docAUROC={np.mean(da):.4f}", flush=True)

"""Scratch verification: reproduce the FROZEN output of the authors' demo.ipynb
(Restaurant Review, bert-base-cased, token-level AUROC = 0.8292 in the notebook)
to validate my rebuilt driver against the authors' released pipeline."""
import os, sys, json, time
import numpy as np

CACHE = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE", ".cache")
HF = os.path.join(CACHE, "hf")
os.environ.setdefault("HF_HOME", HF)
os.environ.setdefault("HF_HUB_DISABLE_SYMLINKS_WARNING", "1")
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
import transformers
transformers.utils.logging.set_verbosity_error()
from src import embed_bert, detector, evaluate

EMB_CACHE = os.path.join(CACHE, "grammar_emb")


def load_docs(name):
    raw = np.load(f"repo/data/{name}.npy", allow_pickle=True).item()
    docs = []
    for i, (tokens, labels) in enumerate(zip(raw["tokens"], raw["labels"])):
        tokens = [str(t) for t in tokens]
        labels = [int(x) for x in labels]
        docs.append({"doc_id": i, "tokens": tokens, "labels": labels,
                     "doc_label": 1 if any(labels) else 0})
    return docs


def get_emb(name, model_name):
    os.makedirs(EMB_CACHE, exist_ok=True)
    path = os.path.join(EMB_CACHE, f"{name}_{model_name}.npz")
    docs = load_docs(name)
    if os.path.exists(path):
        return docs, np.load(path, allow_pickle=True)["data"].item()
    tok, mdl = embed_bert.load_model(model_name, cache_dir=HF)
    t = time.time()
    emb = embed_bert.embed_documents(docs, tok, mdl)
    print(f"[{name}/{model_name}] {len(emb)} docs embedded in {time.time()-t:.1f}s", flush=True)
    np.savez_compressed(path, data=np.array(emb, dtype=object))
    return docs, emb


def run(docs, emb, seed, protocol):
    by_id = {e["doc_id"]: e for e in emb}
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    n_anom = sum(d["doc_label"] for d in docs)
    if protocol == "50pct_all":
        perm = rng.permutation(len(docs)); k = len(docs) // 2
        train = [d for d in (docs[i] for i in perm[:k]) if d["doc_label"] == 0]
        test = [docs[i] for i in perm[k:]]
    else:
        normal = [d for d in docs if d["doc_label"] == 0]

def split_into_chunks(words, tok, max_len=MAX_LEN):
    """Pack a document's words into word-aligned chunks that fit max_len subwords.

    Documents longer than the model's positional limit must not be truncated:
    truncation silently drops gold words (a real defect - it removed 17 of 131
    gold words in the longest Restaurant Review document).  We instead pack whole
    words into consecutive chunks (max_len-2 subwords each, reserving [CLS]/[SEP]),
    embed every chunk and take the element-wise max over the chunk-level word
    representations, so the mapping to gold words stays 1:1 for every document.
    """
    enc = tok(words, is_split_into_words=True, truncation=False)
    n_sub = {}
    for wid in enc.word_ids(batch_index=0):
        if wid is not None:
            n_sub[wid] = n_sub.get(wid, 0) + 1
    budget = max_len - 2
    chunks, cur, cur_len = [], 0, 0
    for i, w in enumerate(words):
        c = n_sub.get(i, 0)
        if cur_len + c > budget and cur < i:
            chunks.append((cur, i))
            cur, cur_len = i, 0
        cur_len += c
    chunks.append((cur, len(words)))
    return chunks


def embed_documents(docs, tok, mdl, max_len=MAX_LEN, batch_size=BATCH, n_threads=8):
    """Return list of dicts {doc_id, emb [n_words,768], labels, doc_label}."""
    torch.set_num_threads(n_threads)

    # 1) word-aligned chunk jobs (one job for documents that fit whole)
    jobs = []  # (doc_id, start_word, end_word, words)
    for d in docs:
        for a, b in split_into_chunks(d["tokens"], tok, max_len):
            jobs.append((d["doc_id"], a, b, d["tokens"][a:b]))

    # 2) batched forward passes
    pooled = {}
    for start in range(0, len(jobs), batch_size):
        batch = jobs[start : start + batch_size]
        enc = tok(
            [j[3] for j in batch],
            is_split_into_words=True,
            return_tensors="pt",
            truncation=True,
            max_length=max_len,
            padding=True,
        )
        with torch.no_grad():
            out = mdl(input_ids=enc["input_ids"], attention_mask=enc["attention_mask"])
        hidden = out.last_hidden_state.numpy().astype(np.float32)
        for j, (doc_id, a, b, _words) in enumerate(batch):
            word_ids = enc.word_ids(batch_index=j)
            emb, seen = pool_word_units(hidden[j], word_ids, len(_words))
            # a single word longer than the positional limit is the only
            # legitimate way to lose one; guard against silent loss elsewhere
            if not seen.all():
                missing = [i + a for i in np.flatnonzero(~seen)]
                raise AssertionError(
                    f"doc {doc_id}: {int((~seen).sum())} words with no subword unit {missing[:10]}"
                )
            prev = pooled.get(doc_id)
            if prev is None:
                arr = np.zeros((len(docs[doc_id]["tokens"]), emb.shape[1]), dtype=np.float32)
                prev = (arr, np.zeros(len(arr), dtype=bool))
            arr, got = prev
            arr[a:b] = emb
            got[a:b] = True
            pooled[doc_id] = (arr, got)

    # 3) assemble and check 1:1 coverage of the gold words (contract R9)
    results = []
    for d in docs:
        emb, got = pooled[d["doc_id"]]
        assert got.all(), (d["doc_id"], int(got.sum()), len(got))
        assert emb.shape[0] == len(d["tokens"]), (emb.shape, len(d["tokens"]))
        results.append(
            {
                "doc_id": d["doc_id"],
                "emb": emb,
                "labels": d["labels"],
                "doc_label": d["doc_label"],
            }
        )
    return results

"""Scratch: which under-specified choice moves Grammar token AUROC?
Uses cached bert-base-uncased embeddings (R1 backbone, fixed)."""
import os, sys
import numpy as np

CACHE = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE", ".cache")
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
from src import data_grammar, detector, evaluate
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

EMB = os.path.join(CACHE, "grammar_emb", "bert-base-uncased.npz")
docs = data_grammar.load_grammar()
emb = np.load(EMB, allow_pickle=True)["data"].item()
by_id = {e["doc_id"]: e for e in emb}


def run(seed, protocol, mode):
    train, test = data_grammar.split_docs(docs, seed=seed, protocol=protocol)
    bank = np.concatenate([by_id[d["doc_id"]]["emb"] for d in train]).astype(np.float32)
    tests = [by_id[d["doc_id"]] for d in test]
    if mode == "standard":
        sc = StandardScaler().fit(bank)
        bank = sc.transform(bank).astype(np.float32)
    elif mode == "l2norm":
        bank = bank / np.linalg.norm(bank, axis=1, keepdims=True)
    scorer = detector.MemoryBankScorer().fit(bank)
    scores, per_doc_auroc, doc_scores, doc_labels = [], [], [], []
    for e in tests:
        x = e["emb"].astype(np.float32)
        if mode == "standard":
            x = sc.transform(x).astype(np.float32)
        elif mode == "l2norm":
            x = x / np.linalg.norm(x, axis=1, keepdims=True)
        s = scorer.score(x)
        scores.append(s)
        doc_scores.append(float(s.mean()))
        doc_labels.append(e["doc_label"])
        if sum(e["labels"]) > 0:
            per_doc_auroc.append(roc_auc_score(e["labels"], s))
    scores = np.concatenate(scores)
    labels = [y for e in tests for y in e["labels"]]
    tm = evaluate.token_metrics(scores, labels)
    dm = evaluate.doc_metrics(np.array(doc_scores), np.array(doc_labels))
    return tm, float(np.mean(per_doc_auroc)), dm, len(per_doc_auroc)


for mode in ["raw", "standard", "l2norm"]:
    for protocol in ["50pct_normal", "50pct_all"]:
        rows = [run(s, protocol, mode) for s in range(10)]
        au = [r[0]["auroc"] for r in rows]
        ap = [r[0]["auprc"] for r in rows]
        ma = [r[1] for r in rows]
        da = [r[2]["auroc"] for r in rows]
        print(f"{mode:9s} {protocol:12s} microAUROC={np.mean(au):.4f}±{np.std(au):.4f} "
              f"(min {min(au):.3f} max {max(au):.3f}) AUPRC={np.mean(ap):.4f} "
              f"macroAUROC={np.mean(ma):.4f} docAUROC={np.mean(da):.4f}", flush=True)

def author_end_to_end(train, test, tok, mdl, cache_dir, log):
    """Run the AUTHORS' own code path end to end on the repo's grammar .npy:

        align.extract_word_embeddings(...)  ->  repo/TokenCore.py  ->  sklearn AUROC

    Nothing from src/ is used here, so the returned number is the independent
    reference for the token-level AUROC of the same 50/50 split.  It also documents
    what the released code actually does (last hidden state, element-wise max over
    subwords, no L2-normalisation, no standardisation, sklearn NearestNeighbors
    default metric = minkowski p=2 i.e. Euclidean distance).
    """
    import contextlib
    import io

    repo = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "repo")
    if repo not in sys.path:
        sys.path.insert(0, repo)
    from align import extract_word_embeddings  # authors' file, verbatim
    from TokenCore import TokenCore  # authors' file, verbatim

    def get_vectors(docs_):
        # silence the authors' per-sentence alignment logging
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
            sent = extract_word_embeddings(
                model=mdl,
                tokenizer=tok,
                all_tokens=[d["tokens"] for d in docs_],
                all_labels=[d["labels"] for d in docs_],
                model_name="bert-base-uncased",
                local_cache_dir=cache_dir,
                device="cpu",
            )
        X = np.array([w["embedding"] for s in sent for w in s], dtype=np.float32)
        y = np.array([w["label"] for s in sent for w in s], dtype=np.int64)
        assert X.shape[0] == sum(len(d["tokens"]) for d in docs_)
        return X, y

    X_tr, y_tr = get_vectors(train)
    X_te, y_te = get_vectors(test)
    assert y_tr.sum() == 0, "authors' bank must be anomaly-free"
    scorer = TokenCore(n_neighbors=1).fit(X_tr)
    scores = scorer.decision_function(X_te)
    res = {

def named_split(docs, name):
    """Deterministic splits that do not depend on a random seed.

    The release stores documents in a canonical Label-Studio order and
    tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py preserves it verbatim (no shuffling, no
    train/test field): docs 0..269 are the correct (normal) sentences and
    270..299 the 30 incorrect (anomalous) ones.  These splits test whether the
    paper's single number can be reached without any random draw.
    """
    normal = [d for d in docs if d["doc_label"] == 0]
    anom = [d for d in docs if d["doc_label"] == 1]
    if name == "canonical_head":
        # first 135 normal documents in file order = memory bank, everything else tests
        k = len(normal) // 2
        return normal[:k], normal[k:] + anom
    if name == "file_halves":
        # contiguous halves of the released file order
        k = len(docs) // 2
        return docs[:k], docs[k:]
    if name == "length_stratified":
        # rank the normal documents by length, take every second one as the bank
        order = sorted(normal, key=lambda d: (len(d["tokens"]), d["doc_id"]))
        train = [d for i, d in enumerate(order) if i % 2 == 0]
        test = [d for i, d in enumerate(order) if i % 2 == 1] + anom
        return train, test
    raise ValueError(name)

args.content:
"""Parse the paper's own Table 1 so the comparison value is not typed into code.

Table 1 of paper/paper.txt lists 7 methods x {SMS_Spam, Review, Grammar, Average}
x {ROC, PRC}, in two blocks ("Token" and "Document").
"""
import re

ROWS = ("LOF", "iForest", "ECOD", "D.SVDD", "AE", "LUNAR", "TokenCore")
COLS = ("SMS_Spam", "Review", "Grammar", "Average")
NUM = re.compile(r"^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$")


def parse_table1(path="paper/paper.txt"):
    lines = [l.strip() for l in open(path, encoding="utf-8").read().splitlines()]
    start = next(i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if l.startswith("Table 1:"))
    table = {}
    section = None
    i = start
    while i < len(lines):
        l = lines[i]
        if l in ("Token", "Document"):
            section = l
            i += 1
            continue
        if l.startswith("6.1") or l.startswith("Experimental Setup"):
            break
        name = next((r for r in ROWS if l == r or l.startswith(r + " ")), None)
        if name and section:
            vals, k = [], i + 1
            while k < len(lines) and NUM.match(lines[k]) and len(vals) < 8:
                vals.append(float(lines[k]))
                k += 1
            assert len(vals) == 8, (section, name, vals)
            table.setdefault(section, {})[name] = {
                "SMS_Spam": {"roc": vals[0], "prc": vals[1]},
                "Review": {"roc": vals[2], "prc": vals[3]},
                "Grammar": {"roc": vals[4], "prc": vals[5]},
                "Average": {"roc": vals[6], "prc": vals[7]},
            }
            i = k
            continue
        i += 1
    assert "Token" in table and "Document" in table, list(table)
    return table


if __name__ == "__main__":
    t = parse_table1()
    for sec in t:
        for m in t[sec]:
            print(sec, m, t[sec][m]["Grammar"])

def read_tolerance(default=0.02, path="state/plan.json"):
    """Tolerance band, read from the workspace plan/contract instead of hard-coded."""
    import re

    try:
        plan = json.load(open(path, encoding="utf-8"))
        m = re.search(r"([0-9.]+)", str(plan.get("config", {}).get("tolerance", "")))
        if m:
            return float(m.group(1))
    except Exception:
        pass
    return default


def punctuation_diagnostic(docs, embedded, splits, log, primary=0):
    """Cheap diagnostic (does NOT change the main entrypoint): score the same splits
    after deleting punctuation-only word units from both the memory bank and the
    scored test tokens, so the effect of including them is visible."""
    punct = set(".,!?;:'\"()[]-–—`")
    is_punct = lambda t: len(t) > 0 and all(ch in punct for ch in t)
    by_id = {e["doc_id"]: e for e in embedded}
    rows = []
    for label, train, test in splits:
        bank = np.concatenate(
            [by_id[d["doc_id"]]["emb"][[not is_punct(t) for t in by_id[d["doc_id"]]["tokens"]]]
             for d in train])
        scores, labels = [], []
        for d in test:
            e = by_id[d["doc_id"]]
            keep = [not is_punct(t) for t in e["tokens"]]
            sc = detector.MemoryBankScorer().fit(bank).score(e["emb"][keep])
            scores.append(sc)
            labels.extend([y for y, k in zip(e["labels"], keep) if k])
        tm = evaluate.token_metrics(np.concatenate(scores), labels)
        rows.append({"split": label, "token_auroc": tm["auroc"], "token_auprc": tm["auprc"],
                     "n_bank_tokens": int(bank.shape[0]), "n_tokens": tm["n_tokens"],
                     "n_positive_tokens": tm["n_positive_tokens"]})
    aurocs = [r["token_auroc"] for r in rows]
    log(f"[diagnostic:no-punctuation] token AUROC mean={np.mean(aurocs):.4f} "
        f"std={np.std(aurocs):.4f} over {len(rows)} splits "
        f"(primary {rows[primary]['split']}: {rows[primary]['token_auroc']:.4f})")
    return {
        "description": ("punctuation-only word units removed from the memory bank and from the "
                        "scored test tokens (diagnostic only; the reported pipeline keeps them)"),
        "token_auroc_mean": float(np.mean(aurocs)),
        "token_auroc_std": float(np.std(aurocs)),
        "token_auprc_mean": float(np.mean([r["token_auprc"] for r in rows])),
        "per_split": rows,
    }

target.statement: TokenCore token-level AUROC on the Grammar dataset
target.table_ref: Table 1, Token section, row TokenCore, column Grammar ROC

tolerance.why: Rule 3: AUROC is a bounded score and the paper prints it in [0,1] as a fraction; no std/CI over repeated runs is reported (rule 1 inapplicable), and the token-level test set for Grammar is only ~150 documents' tokens, whose size is never stated as 2,000+ examples, so the smaller-set band of 0.02 absolute is used rather than the 0.01 of rule 2.

audit_summary: The pipeline is a faithful implementation of TokenCore on the Grammar benchmark: BERT-base-uncased last hidden state, element-wise max pooling over subwords, memory bank of the 50% normal training documents only, nearest-neighbour (Euclidean) token distance, mean document aggregation, micro token-level AUROC/AUPRC - and it is bit-identical to the authors' released align.py + TokenCore.py (|diff| = 0, alignment parity 3e-6). The full 300-document, 2746-token, 47-positive-token benchmark was used with all 10 seeds; nothing was subsampled, so scaled_down is false. The reported seed-0 token AUROC is 0.6053 vs the paper's 0.6371 (delta -0.032, outside the 0.02 band); the 10-seed mean is 0.586 +/- 0.021, so the shortfall is not a single unlucky draw but a systematic gap under the 50pct_normal protocol. The dominant cause is that the paper's actual split is unreleased (eval.split_anomaly_data absent from the repo) and the paper never states the seed, the sampled sentences, punctuation handling, or the aggregation of token AUROC; the authors' own demo used bert-base-cased, while R1 mandates bert-base-uncased. The comparison set (LOF/iForest/ECOD/DeepSVDD/AE/LUNAR) was not run - only the Table 1 numbers were parsed for reference - so R8 is missing, though that does not affect the match target's method. No hard-coded or echoed numbers: the paper value is parsed from paper/paper.txt via paper_ref.py and all reported metrics come from sklearn on computed scores.
